description: Capture an idea as a Backlog task. The next plan run will triage and scope it. Use anytime to log bugs, feature requests, or improvements without interrupting the current cycle. IMPORTANT: If this idea originates from a research or planning session, you MUST include a Reference: line in notes pointing to the source doc. Without it, the planner has no context and will misinterpret the intent. Does not call the Anthropic API.

acceptance.description: Optional definition of success. Rendered under ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.

complexity.description: Estimated complexity. XS = config/one-liner. Small = one file. Medium = 2-5 files. Large = cross-module. XL = architectural. Default: "Small".

conflicts_with_ad.description: The Active Decision this idea cuts against, e.g. "AD-12". USE THIS INSTEAD OF DROPPING THE IDEA. An AD is *active* — it can be superseded — so a contradiction is a decision for the user, never a reason for you to shelve work during research or scoping. The task is created and parked Blocked behind a decision-gate on that AD: it shows in `orient` as a decision waiting on the owner, and returns to the board automatically once the AD is superseded, modified, or reaffirmed.

discovery.description: When true, classify the idea and route to Discovery Canvas instead of backlog. Default: false (always creates a backlog task).

do.description: Optional scope: what this idea should do. Rendered under SCOPE (DO THIS).

do_not.description: Optional boundary: what this idea must not do. Rendered under SCOPE BOUNDARY (DO NOT DO THIS).

doc_ref.description: Path to a reference document (e.g. "docs/research/foo.md"). Stored as a structured field — replaces the fragile "Reference:" line in notes.

force.description: Force creation even if a high-overlap duplicate or already-done task is detected. Default: false.

notes.description: Additional context, constraints, or reasoning. Notes are trimmed and capped at 2,000 Unicode characters for the write path; overflow is marked on the stored record and the omitted remainder is returned so it can be recovered in the same call. MANDATORY: If this idea comes from a research or planning session, include a "Reference: <path>" line pointing to the source doc. Tasks submitted without references get misinterpreted by the planner — this is the #1 cause of wasted build slots (C146: task-807 was scoped as landing page copy when it was actually a dashboard UX task, because the source research doc was missing). Use doc_search to find relevant docs before submitting. TIP: If this idea addresses a known cycle learning, include "learning:<uuid>" in the notes (e.g. "learning:abc12345-..."). This links the idea to the learning entry and marks it actioned in the pipeline. Example: "Addresses recurring friction. learning:3f9a1c2e-..."

opportunity.description: What user problem does this solve? Auto-fill from problem context in notes when submitting ideas that describe a user pain point. The planner uses this to cluster backlog tasks by opportunity.

priority.description: Priority level. P0 = broken/blocking. P1 = strategically aligned with current goals. P2 = valuable but not urgent. P3 = nice-to-have/speculative. Default: "P2 Medium". Assess based on strategic alignment and impact, not just effort.

project.description: Project id (UUID) or slug to write this idea to, overriding the session project for THIS call only. Must be a project on your account — fails closed otherwise. Use project_switch to change the session default. PASS THIS WHENEVER YOU KNOW WHICH REPO THE SESSION IS IN: on a multi-project account a connection with no project bound cannot be resolved, and PAPI will stop and ask rather than guess.

proposal.description: task-4001: OPTIONAL. Propose a Decision or a Convention you settled while raising this idea. PAPI never mints one for you — a proposal passing all four admission tests is QUEUED for the owner behind a decision gate, and nothing is written as an Active Decision. YOU apply the four tests (the AD Admission Rule states them); the server routes on your answers and makes no judgement about the content. Same shape as build_execute's `proposal`.

body.description: What was decided or settled, and why.

module.description: Optional module scope. Only used when this lands as a Convention.

tests.description: The four admission tests, each answered explicitly. An omitted test is NOT a failed test.

alternativesWereReal.description: (a) Something else could genuinely have been chosen.

arguableToday.description: (c) A competent person could argue the other side right now.

constrainsFutureWork.description: (b) It changes what a task nobody has written yet will do.

reversalCostsMore.description: (d) Reversing it costs more than making it did.

title.description: One line stating the stance or rule.

relationship.description: Optional relationship to existing work, system, or user problem. Rendered under RELATIONSHIP.

scope_class.description: AD-29 scope class (default: inferred from complexity — L/XL becomes a brief). ALSO the owner-action routing override: when you set scope_class='task' EXPLICITLY, an idea that would otherwise be misrouted to the Owner Action Queue by a word in its title (e.g. "send", "call", "contract") is filed to the build backlog instead. Use it when the classifier hijacks an ordinary engineering task.

text.description: The idea — becomes the task title.

type.description: Task type. Defaults to "task". Use "bug" for defects, "research" for investigation tasks, "spike" for time-boxed experiments, "discovery" for issues found during a build that need their own task. The planner uses this to generate type-specific BUILD HANDOFFs.

name: idea
